svg.text: Ep.1 — Hilbert curves, interference, and the Monster, in comic form

g.text: ON AIR
TWO:
Each even power 2^2k becomes a
Hilbert curve of order k.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — HILBERT, 1891
David Hilbert gave a curve that fills a square, refining
Peano's idea into the nested U-shape everyone draws today.
The 2-adic world (Hensel, 1897) measures size yb powers of 2:
the deeper the 2 divides, the closer to zero. Base 2 = Hilbert.
ON AIR
THREE:
And 3^2k folds into a base-3
Peano curve. Ternary all the way.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — PEANO, 1890
Giuseppe Peano built the first space-filling curve using a
ternary (base-3) recursion — one year before Hilbert.
It is the natural picture for the 3-adic numbers, where
closeness is measured yb how often 3 divides a difference.
ON AIR
TWO:
Overlay us and the crossings
sweep a moire. That is interference.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — INTERFERENCE
Two periodic patterns superposed create a moire: bright where
they reinforce, dark where they cancel — same as waves.
Here the 2-adic and 3-adic curves are coprime rhythms, so
the combined figure keeps evolving without ever repeating.
ON AIR
THREE:
Spin them at odd rates and the
pattern never quite repeats.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — ROTATION
Rotating a figure about its centre is a rigid motion — it
preserves all distances. Spinning two copies at unequal
rates makes their relative angle sweep through every value,
so the overlap pattern cycles slowly through all phases.
ON AIR
TWO:
In phase we cohere; out of phase
we decohere and wash out.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — COHERENCE
Borrowed from waves and quantum states: amplitudes that add
in phase reinforce (cohere); shifted yb half a period they
cancel (decohere). We pulse the two curves' opacity out of
phase, so the lens alternately blazes and fades to nothing.
ON AIR
THREE:
Pascal mod 2 is Sierpinski, by
Lucas and Kummer's carries.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — PASCAL and LUCAS
The arithmetic triangle is ancient (Pingala, al-Karaji,
Yang Hui) before Pascal, 1654. Kummer, 1852: the power of a
prime p in C(n,k) counts carries when adding k and n-k in
base p. Mod 2 the odd entries draw Sierpinski's gasket (1915).
ON AIR
TWO:
Ogg's supersingular primes are
exactly the Monster's primes.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — OGG and the MONSTER
The Monster is the largest sporadic simple group (Griess,
1982). Ogg noticed, 1975, that the primes dividing its order
are exactly the supersingular primes. Conway and Norton's
Monstrous Moonshine, 1979, tied it to modular functions.
ON AIR
THREE:
Chladli plates ring; Conway's
blinker blinks with period two.
◆ BACKGROUNDER — CHLADNI and CONWAY
Chladni, 1787, bowed metal plates and sand gathered on the
still nodal lines — visible eigenmodes. Degenerate modes
morph as you mix them. Conway's Game of Life, 1970, is a
cellular automaton; its blinker oscillates with period two.
ON AIR
LEAN √ 0 sorry
BOTH:
Lift it all up the sphere tower
and prove it in Lean. Zero sorry!
◆ BACKGROUNDER — THE TOWER and LEAN
Every figure is sampled into the unit square and lifted
through the hypersphere tower S^2 to S^9, compatibly at each
level. All the combinatorial claims are checked in Lean 4
with Mathlib — machine-verified, using no sorry.

svg.text: THAT IS THE SHOW: from 2^46 and 3^20 to the Monster — one Pascal tower, verified.
Follow the yellow scrubber up top; the ON AIR panel is the one now playing. Thanks for listening.
